title: Patch-Based Feature Extraction for Machine Learning
text: common machine learning preprocessing step large images split fixed-size patches, run patch feature extractor (e.g. pretrained CNN), collect resulting embeddings downstream analysis. naive approach — loading model inside FUN, per patch — prohibitively slow. Model initialization typically takes several seconds, image 10,000 patches overhead dominates costs. tilework solves two mechanisms: setup_FUN — runs per worker batch processing begins. output passed every FUN call via .SETUP_OUT. Batched iteration — tileIterator groups patches batches, model processes many patches per forward pass rather one time.

code: .predict_group <- function(x, tg, batch_size, group) {     iter <- tileIterator(tg, batch_size = batch_size, active_group = group)      tileApply(         x,         tiles = iter,         setup_FUN = function(.X) {             # Peek at the first tile to learn the expected input shape             # without advancing the iterator position.             first_tile <- getTile(.X, iter, advance = FALSE)[[1L]]             input_shape <- c(dim(first_tile)[1:2], terra::nlyr(.X))             mock_feature_extractor(input_shape)         },         FUN = function(batch, .I, .SETUP_OUT) {             model <- .SETUP_OUT              # Convert batch to (n, h, w, c) array             arr <- do.call(                 abind::abind,                 c(lapply(batch, terra::as.array), along = 4L)             )             arr <- aperm(arr, c(4L, 1L, 2L, 3L))              # Run inference             p <- model$predict(arr)   # n_features x n_tiles             colnames(p) <- .I         # label each column with its tile index             p         }     ) }

title: Selecting, Grouping, and Iterating Tiles
text: tileGroup organises tiles plan named groups. group logical partition — groups can overlap, tiles need assigned group. Groups accept indexing styles underlying plan, can mixed within tileGroup: Vector indexing — flat integer vector tile indices. ij indexing — list(rows, cols) selects grid position, expanding row × col combinations. list(2:(nr-1), 2:(nc-1)) means interior rows × interior cols.
code: nr <- nrow(tp) nc <- ncol(tp)  tg <- tileGroup(tp, groups = list(     interior = list(2:(nr - 1L), 2:(nc - 1L)),  # ij indexing     border   = c(                                 # vector indexing         # top and bottom rows         seq_len(nc),         seq(length(tp) - nc + 1L, length(tp)),         # left and right columns (excluding corners)         seq(nc + 1L, length(tp) - nc, by = nc),         seq(nc + nc, length(tp) - 1L, by = nc)     ) ))  tg #> <tileGroup>: pixelTilePlan #> groups------------------------- #>   interior : 9 tiles #>   border   : 16 tiles

title: Selecting, Grouping, and Iterating Tiles
text: tileApply tileGroup accepts parallel_strategy argument: "groups" (default) — groups distributed across workers. worker processes tiles assigned group sequentially. right choice : Groups meaningfully different processing logic Per-worker setup cost significant (model loading, DB connection) — use setup_FUN runs per group/worker Groups large enough keep workers busy "tiles" — groups processed sequentially, tiles within group distributed across workers. right choice : tile expensive independent Groups tiles per group many Per-worker setup cost low (setup_FUN available )

title: Choosing and Creating a Tile Plan
text: tilework provides four concrete tile plan classes, suited different way thinking dataset divided: choice usually straightforward: Working georeferenced rasters vectors coordinates CRS units? → spatialTilePlan Working images pixel position matters? → pixelTilePlan list locations (cell centroids, tissue landmarks, sample sites) want extract fixed-size patches around? → pointTilePlan Need variable-size tiles driven data density external partitioning algorithm? → freeTilePlan (often via quadtreePlan())

title: Choosing and Creating a Tile Plan
text: spatialTilePlan divides spatial extent uniform grid. Tile bounds returned SpatExtent objects, route directly terra’s spatial windowing operations downstream. Two things required: extent tile count request. actual number tiles generated least requested number, arranged squarely possible given extent’s aspect ratio.  Padding expands tile’s bounds equally four sides extraction time. plan’s extent affected.  Indexing returns SpatExtent objects: use: workflow tile bounds need expressed coordinate system data — georeferenced rasters, sf geometries, SpatVector objects.
code: tp_spat <- spatialTilePlan(ext = c(0, 1000, 0, 600), n = 12)  tp_spat #> Object of class spatialTilePlan  #> extent : 0, 1000, 0, 600 (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax) #> dim    : 3 4 #> pad    : 0 dim(tp_spat)   # nrow x ncol of the tile grid #> [1] 3 4 length(tp_spat) #> [1] 12 plot(tp_spat) tp_spat_padded <- tp_spat + 20 plot(tp_spat_padded, alpha = 0.4) tp_spat[1]       # first tile #> [[1]] #> SpatExtent : 0, 250, 0, 200 (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax) tp_spat[2, 3]    # row 2, col 3 #> [[1]] #> SpatExtent : 500, 750, 200, 400 (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax)

title: Choosing and Creating a Tile Plan
text: pixelTilePlan divides image uniform grid pixel-exact tiles. Bounds returned integer[4] vectors c(xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax) pixel index space, routing array/matrix subsetting operations downstream. Three things required: image’s pixel dimensions (pxdims), tile height width pixels (nrows, ncols).  Padding pixel plans automatically zeroed top-left corner padded tiles first row/column produce negative indices. use: Image processing workflows meaningful spatial coordinate system — microscopy images, whole slide images, general computer vision pipelines. Also right choice pixel-exact tile boundaries matter (e.g. ML patch extraction tile size must match model input exactly).
code: tp_px <- pixelTilePlan(pxdims = c(500, 800), nrows = 100, ncols = 100)  tp_px #> Object of class pixelTilePlan  #> tiles  : 40 #> pxdim  : 500, 800 #> pxrows : 100 #> pxcol  : 100 #> dim    : 5, 8 #> pad    : 0 dim(tp_px) #> [1] 5 8 length(tp_px) #> [1] 40 plot(tp_px) tp_px_padded <- tp_px + 5 tp_px_padded[1]   # first tile: note xmin/ymin are still >= 1 #> [[1]] #> [1]   1 110   1 110 #> attr(,"tile") #> [1] 1 tp_px[1]          # unpadded for comparison #> [[1]] #> [1]   1 100   1 100 #> attr(,"tile") #> [1] 1

text: common workflow let quadtreePlan() build freeTilePlan automatically. starts coarse tilePlan, applies FUN tile, recursively splits tiles whose value exceeds threshold. Splitting continues tiles threshold, smaller min_tile_size, max_depth reached. splitting, neighboring leaf tiles whose combined FUN value stays ≤ threshold merged back single rectangle, reducing tile count sparse regions. FUN must return single numeric scalar per tile — typically count, density, variance. last measured value leaf stored n_records metadata column.  High-density regions subdivided many small tiles; sparse regions remain large tiles (merged back neighbors also sparse). n_records records point count leaf:  resulting freeTilePlan standard tilePlan works tileApply(), tileIterator, tileGroup like . use: Vector/point data density varies strongly across space. workflow uniform grid waste computation empty regions exceed memory limits dense regions. output external space-partitioning step (pass bounds directly via $bounds<-). title: Choosing and Creating a Tile Plan
text: Regardless plan type, two practical considerations apply: Tile size controls memory footprint per tile , ML workflows, chosen model’s expected input dimensions mind. Larger tiles mean fewer total tiles memory per tile. natural tile size match model input exactly, terra::aggregate() terra::resample() can resize extracted tile inside FUN rather constraining tile plan . Padding handles edge effects operations need spatial context (convolutions, focal statistics, buffer-based extractions). pad value least large half-width operation’s kernel buffer radius. pixel plans, padding zero-clamped image edges; spatial plans extends beyond plan extent, shrink plan extent inward pad amount want tiles stay within data boundary.
code: tp_demo <- spatialTilePlan(ext = c(0, 100, 0, 100), n = 9)  # shrink extent inward by pad so padded tiles stay within data pad <- 3 ext(tp_demo) <- ext(tp_demo) - pad tp_demo <- tp_demo + pad  plot(tp_demo, alpha = 0.4) plot(ext(c(0, 100, 0, 100)), add = TRUE, border = "red")
